UntrashOS on the Zyxel NAS542 — User Guide

Installation and operation of UntrashOS on the Zyxel NAS542

This guide covers installing UntrashOS from the USB stick and every function of the Untrash Desk, the web interface you use to run the NAS. Each screen is described with all of its options. The tables list each option, its choices (the default is bold), and what it does.

About the screenshots. The screenshots were taken on emulated hardware: the installer runs in its dry run (commands are shown, not executed), and the Desk runs in a test mode with example data. All names, addresses and files are examples (users anna and ben, network 192.0.2.x, *.example.net). The procedures themselves (stick installation under the Zyxel firmware, return to stock, updates) have been run on real NAS542 hardware.

The guide is also built into UntrashOS: open Manual in the Desk, use the link on the sign-in page, or the link at the top of the installer. All of them offer this guide as a PDF as well.

1. Installation

1.1 What you need

  • A Zyxel NAS542 running the original Zyxel firmware, with its disks in place.
  • A USB stick of at least 4 GB (the image is 3.4 GB). It is erased.
  • A PC, tablet or phone with a web browser on the same network as the NAS.
  • The UntrashOS stick image untrash-stick-<version>.img.

1.2 Write the stick

Write the image to the stick with any image writer (balenaEtcher, Raspberry Pi Imager, dd). On Linux, the project script does the same with extra checks. Replace /dev/sdX with your stick. Every byte on that device is overwritten:

sudo os/install/write-stick.sh untrash-stick-<version>.img /dev/sdX

The stick image is the same for every NAS542. Nothing on it is made for a particular device. Everything that belongs to one NAS is created on that NAS during the first run. The stick then holds that NAS's backup and is marked as used. Use a freshly written stick for each NAS.

1.3 First run under the Zyxel firmware

  1. Switch the NAS off and plug the stick into a USB port of the NAS.
  2. Switch the NAS on. While it starts, the Zyxel firmware runs the install script from the stick:
    1. It checks that the flash layout and the boot settings are those of a normal NAS542.
    2. It saves a complete backup of the flash to the stick, reads it back and compares it.
    3. It saves the Zyxel configuration (users, groups, shares, passwords) to the stick.
    4. It installs the small UntrashOS loader into the unused one of the two firmware slots and adds one call to the boot settings. The Zyxel firmware itself is not changed.
    5. It switches the NAS off.
  3. Leave the stick in the NAS.

If any step fails, the script writes the backup back, leaves an INSTALL_FAILED marker on the stick and switches the NAS off. The NAS then starts the Zyxel firmware as before.

1.4 Open the installer

Switch the NAS on again. The loader starts the installer from the stick. After a minute or two, open

http://zyxel-untrash.local/ in the browser. If your router does not resolve .local names, try http://zyxel-untrash/ or the address your router lists for the NAS.

Element Meaning
Stick Model and size of the installation stick.
System image The UntrashOS version on the stick. Missing means the stick image is incomplete.
Stock backup present, checked: the flash backup was read back and compared when it was made. present (unchecked): the backup exists but was not compared. No stock backup: way D is not possible.
Stock configuration on the stick The saved Zyxel users, groups and shares, needed for way B.
Disk table Every disk with size, model and content: Zyxel-Stock (a disk of the Zyxel firmware), empty, UntrashOS, RAID member or unknown.
Language (top right) Deutsch, English, Français. The installed system starts with the language chosen here.
User guide (top) Opens this guide.

1.5 The four ways

There are four ways. Ways B and C keep all your data. They change no partition and no RAID array. UntrashOS is stored as a few files in the hidden folder /.untrash of an existing Zyxel volume. Only way A erases a disk.

Way What happens Data Confirmation word
B – Keep and take over New installation on a Zyxel volume. Users, groups, shares and SMB passwords of the Zyxel firmware are taken over on the first start. kept BEHALTEN
C – Keep, set up anew New installation on a Zyxel volume. A new admin password and a network name are set. Every top-level folder becomes a share for admin. The old users are not taken over. kept BEHALTEN
A – Erase the disk and reinstall The chosen disk is erased and gets its own UntrashOS layout (two system slots, state, swap, data area with btrfs). erased on that disk LÖSCHEN <disk>, e.g. LÖSCHEN sdc
D – Back to the stock firmware Writes the Zyxel boot data back from the backup on the stick (see section 18). kept STOCK

Choosing a way shows its plan, step by step. Nothing happens until you confirm:

  1. Type the confirmation word shown in the yellow box and click Start.
  2. Press the COPY button on the front of the NAS within 60 seconds. Without the button press, the installer stops and changes nothing.

Way B options

Option Choices Meaning
Volume the Zyxel volumes, system volume first Where the UntrashOS files go. The installer shows the free space. It needs room for two copies of the system image plus 5 GiB.
Stock configuration (expandable) Shows the groups, users and shares that will be taken over.

Way C options

Option Choices Meaning
Volume as for way B Where the UntrashOS files go.
Network name text, default zyxel-untrash 1–15 letters, digits or hyphens. The NAS is reachable as <name>.local.
New password for admin text At least 8 characters. Used for the Desk, SMB and SSH.
Repeat password text Must match.

Way A options

Option Choices Meaning
Disk every disk with size, model and content The disk to erase. It needs at least 16 GiB. The disk the installer itself runs from cannot be chosen. If the disk belongs to a Zyxel RAID array, the plan warns that the array loses a disk.

Way D options

Option Choices Meaning
Backup the completed installation backups on the stick, newest first The state the NAS returns to.

The installer refuses to start when a requirement is missing, and says why. Examples: no stick or no system image, too little free space on the volume, an incomplete RAID array ("insert all disks first"), a disk that already carries UntrashOS partitions while you choose way B or C.

1.6 Progress and restart

The Progress box shows the state (ready, COPY button, running, done, error) and logs every step and command. Before anything is written, the partition tables and RAID/LVM metadata of the affected disks are saved to the stick (UNTRASH/disk-backup-…). Every system image that is written is read back and compared.

When the state is done, click Restart. The NAS starts the installed UntrashOS. You can remove the stick afterwards. Keep it: it holds the backup for the way back to the Zyxel firmware.

The yellow Dry run box and (DRY RUN) in the screenshot exist only in the emulation used for this guide.

Open http://<network name>.local/ (for example http://zyxel-untrash.local/), or the address of the NAS.

After way A the NAS has no users yet. The first page asks for:

Password for admin At least 8 characters.
Repeat password Must match.

After way B or C, sign in. After way B, every user keeps the password from the Zyxel firmware. After way C, use admin and the password you chose in the installer.

Option Meaning
Language Language of this browser: Deutsch, English, Français.
User name, Password Your account. Several wrong passwords in a row lock the sign-in for a while.

3. Working with the Desk

Element Meaning
Top bar Name of the active window; current activity (for example a media scan, streams, a running backup or update); RAID state; your user name (click it to change the language of this browser or to sign out); date and time.
Desktop icons The first apps, opened with a click.
Dock All apps. Hover over an icon to see its name. The power button at the right end switches the NAS off or restarts it (section 16).
Windows Move them by the title bar and resize them at the edges and corners. ▢ maximizes, and so does a double click on the title bar. ✕ closes. Each window keeps its size in your browser.

Administrators see all apps. Normal users see Files, Channels, Manual and My account (section 17).

Converting runs in the background and is slow on the NAS, which has no hardware encoder: a feature film in 720p takes several hours. The top bar and Exports show the progress.

6. Storage

Volumes and RAID lists each array with its RAID type, size, disks, state (healthy, degraded, resyncing, failed) and its volumes with their fill level. Drive lists every disk with bay, size, model, SMART state, temperature and role (in the RAID, free, free (old data), UntrashOS, USB). All volumes are created in the format of the Zyxel firmware, so the Zyxel firmware can still read them after the way back.

Action What it does Confirmation
+ New volume New array on free disks, see below. FORMATIEREN
Rename New name for the volume. —
Add disks Extends the array with free disks; the RAID type stays. FORMATIEREN
Change RAID type Moves to the next RAID type (for example RAID 1 → RAID 5) with additional disks. FORMATIEREN
Spare disk Adds a hot spare that takes over when a disk fails. FORMATIEREN
Repair (only for degraded arrays) Rebuilds the array onto a free disk. FORMATIEREN
Extend After swapping all disks for larger ones: grows the array and file system to the new size. —
Delete Deletes the volume and every share on it. LÖSCHEN

The confirmation word protects the disks: everything on the selected disks, or on the deleted volume, is lost. A running job is shown with its progress and log.

RAID 0: striped, fast, no redundancy. RAID 1: mirrored. RAID 5: survives one failed disk. RAID 6: survives two. RAID 10: mirrored and striped.

Router (UPnP port forwarding) opens ports on the router for access from the internet. 10. Ad filter

The ad filter blocks ads and trackers for every device in the home network that uses the NAS as its DNS server.

Page Content and options
Overview Switch on/off; queries and blocked queries in the last 24 hours, share blocked, devices; a chart of the last 24 hours; most blocked and most requested domains; the devices.
Log Single queries. Filter by domain or device, blocked only (off). Each entry can be allowed or blocked directly.
Lists The block lists in use, each can be switched on/off or removed. Built in: StevenBlack (on), Hagezi Light, Hagezi Pro (stricter). Add your own list with Name and List address (hosts or domain format). Update now reloads the lists; they also reload every week.
Own rules Always allow and Always block, one domain per line. A blocked domain includes all its subdomains. Always allow wins over the lists.
Setup How to make the devices use the NAS as DNS server, see below.

Setup in short: in the router, enter the address of the NAS as the local DNS server (on a FRITZ!Box: Home Network → Network → Network Settings → IPv4 Settings). Then reconnect the devices. The NAS needs a fixed address for this (in the router: "always assign the same IPv4 address", or a static address in section 8). While the NAS is off, devices cannot resolve names until the router falls back to its own DNS, and some routers do not. Single devices can also be switched in their own network settings.

More lists block more, but also more likely something you want. Then add that domain to Always allow.

11. Media server and channels

Media server

The media server (DLNA/UPnP) makes videos, music and photos available to TVs, consoles, VLC and Kodi. It appears in the network under the host name of the NAS.

Page Content and options
Status State (on/off); number of videos, songs and photos; devices that asked; current playbacks; Rescan reads all shares again.
Shares Per share: Video, Photos, Music. Empty or missing folders are not published. (The same as in Shares.)
Channels The channels, see below.
Settings Media server on (off); Channels receivable in the home network without signing in (on, for TVs, VLC, Kodi).

Channels

A channel works like a TV station: it plays its playlist endlessly by the clock, and everyone who tunes in sees the same thing. The NAS converts a channel only once, however many people watch it, and at most 2 channels at the same time. A channel starts with its first viewer and pauses one minute after the last one leaves.

Option Choices Meaning
Name text Name of the channel.
Type Video 480p (little CPU), Video 720p (more CPU), Video unchanged (H.264 only, hardly any CPU), Radio (sound only) Picture quality versus load on the NAS.
Random order off, on Shuffles the playlist, the same way for every viewer.
Shares / Playlist files and folders of the shares Add videos, music or whole folders (+). Folders play everything inside them, including subfolders, in name order. Reorder with ↑, remove with ✕.

Everyone watches in the Channels app (also in the dock of normal users). The list of channels is also available as an M3U playlist for VLC and Kodi (Channel list (M3U)).

+ Backup creates a backup job. The list shows each job with type, target, schedule and last run. Each job can be started at once (Now), edited or deleted. Restore copies a backup back.

Option Choices Meaning
Name text

Sources shares, each with an optional folder (empty = whole share); + Source adds more What is backed up.
Target Share on this NAS (share and folder), connected USB drives Where it goes (archive and synchronization).
Rsync server, Module, User name, Password only for Rsync server The rsync target. An empty password keeps the saved one.
Schedule manual only, hourly, daily, weekly, monthly; Time 02:00; Weekday; Day of month When the job runs.
Keep versions (archive) default 7 Older versions are deleted.
Bandwidth KB/s 0 = unlimited Limits the speed.
Active on, off Off keeps the job without running it on schedule.

Restore (archive and synchronization jobs): choose a version, the share to restore into and a folder (default Restored). The backup is copied into that folder.

15. Updates

The page shows the installed version and the system slot it runs from (A or B).

  1. Click Choose a system image … and select an update file (untrash-…-update.utslot). A stick image (.img) is refused.
  2. The file is uploaded (with progress) and checked: signature and checksums.
  3. Click Install: the image is written to the other slot.
  4. Click Restart now.

If the new system does not start cleanly, the loader goes back to the current one by itself. Your settings and data are not part of the slot and stay as they are.

16. Status, logs and system tools

Status is updated every two seconds:

Element Meaning
Rings CPU in total and per core, memory, case temperature. Colours change at warning levels.
Disks Temperature of each disk. Sleeping disks are shown as asleep and are not woken up.
Network Current traffic per port.
Bottom line Load, fan level, uptime, swap in use.

Logs shows the system log or the log of a single service: System, SMB, Volumes, Takeover (the first start after way B), SSH, FTP, Media server, Desk.

Sounds edits the melodies the NAS buzzer plays for events: Start, Shut down, Error, Critical, Success, Device connected, Device disconnected, Warning, Standby. Events you changed are marked ★.

Option Meaning
Tempo 25–400 %. Above 100 % notes get slower and longer.
Tone table Each row is a tone: name (C6, A#5, Bb4, or Pause), frequency in Hz, length in ms. ↑ moves a row, + inserts, ✕ deletes.
+ Tone, + Pause Adds a row at the end.
▶ In the browser, ▶ On the NAS, ■ Plays the melody, or stops it.
Save, Back to built-in Saves your melody, or returns to the original.
Import sound set, Export as sound set Loads or saves all melodies as a JSON file.

Terminal (administrators only) opens a shell on the NAS in the browser window.

UntrashMesh is a preview of a coming feature: several UntrashOS devices form one encrypted network for mirrored shares, mutual off-site backups and access on the road. It will arrive with an update.

Feedback prepares a bug report or a suggestion as a GitHub issue. Nothing is sent automatically.

Option Choices Meaning
Kind Error, Suggestion
Title, Description text What happened, what you expected, how to reproduce it.
Attach anonymised system info on, off Version, kernel, disks, RAID, services and recent error messages, without addresses or names. Preview shows exactly what is attached.
Copy text, Open on GitHub Copies the text, or opens it as a prepared issue on GitHub. You check it and submit it yourself (GitHub account needed).

Manual shows this guide inside the Desk, with Open in a new tab and Download PDF:

Power button (end of the dock): Run switches the NAS off. With Restart instead it restarts. All connections are closed.

Your user name (top bar): change the language of this browser (— as system —, Deutsch, English, Français) or Sign out.

17. Working as a normal user

Users who are not administrators see a smaller Desk: Files, Channels, Manual and My account. They see only the shares they have rights to and can only change what those rights allow.

My account: Current password, New password, Repeat, then Change password. Sign out ends the session.

18. Back to the Zyxel firmware

UntrashOS can always go back to the original Zyxel firmware with the backup on the installation stick. Data on the disks stays. The UntrashOS files in /.untrash (ways B and C) or the UntrashOS disk (way A) are left in place, so you can return to UntrashOS later.

From the Desk: plug in the installation stick, open Settings → Back to stock. The page shows the backup found on the stick. Type STOCK and click Back to the Zyxel firmware.

From the installer (if UntrashOS does not start any more): start the NAS with the installation stick and choose way D.

Both ways then do the same:

  1. The backup is checked against its checksums, and the stick gets the ROLLBACK order.
  2. The NAS restarts and runs the Zyxel firmware once. The firmware writes its boot data back from the backup and switches the NAS off after a few minutes. Leave the stick in.
  3. Switch the NAS on: it starts the Zyxel firmware as before the installation.
